title: Fragmented Spirit
identity: Stacy Garrop’s Fragmented Spirit is Theodore Presser 114-41106 for E-flat alto saxophone and piano, 28 pages, listed at 7:30 by the retailer and Presser. The public Sheet Music Plus preview was opened and displays only the cover, without notation. Noa Even’s performer repertoire listing gives a different timing, about 8:20; it remains a performance-specific estimate.

evidence.claim: Retailer listing verifies the exact Presser item, scoring, extent and advertised duration; the advertised preview was opened and visually showed only the cover, not notation.
Noa Even repertoire page lists the saxophone and piano version at about 8:20.
Naxos library record credits Michael Duke, saxophone, and David Howie, piano, on a 2012 recording.
UT Austin master's recital repository record includes the work.
evidence.source_name: University of Texas at Austin repository

evidence.claim: A 2000 UNCG Saxophone Studio page lists Fragmented Spirit among repertoire supported by its SmartMusic accompaniment project; this documents a university practice resource, not placement on a degree recital or difficulty level.

Noa Even’s solo-with-piano repertoire page lists the alto saxophone and piano work at about 8:20, differing from Presser/SMP’s 7:30 listing; these are source-specific timings, not a score-duration correction.

review_focus: The retailer attributes a “mini-drama” description and “new and faster landscapes” to the composer; because that text is derivative retailer copy, treat it only as a lead and assess pacing and character from the actual score.
collection_flag: A University of Texas master’s recital record includes the work, and a UNCG studio page lists it in a saxophone accompaniment resource. These are documented college-use contexts, not level assignments.

listening.description: Michael Duke and David Howie recording, track listing 9:15.
listening.verification: Catalog credits and runtime verified; playback not auditioned.

score_links.description: Advertised public preview opened; cover page only, with no notation.
